source: Changes to the feature values built from PanPhon, Hayes (2009) and the IPA vowel chart, each with the source that decides it.

overrides.source: Hayes (2009), Introductory Phonology, as converted to CSV by Gorman (github.com/kylebgorman/hayes2009, dataprep/Features.csv)
overrides.reason: Hayes gives the alveolar approximant no tongue-body value; PanPhon's [+high] describes the English bunched r, not the symbol.

overrides.source: Hayes (2009), Introductory Phonology, as converted to CSV by Gorman (github.com/kylebgorman/hayes2009, dataprep/Features.csv)
overrides.reason: Hayes gives [ɹ] [-round]; the IPA chart symbol carries no lip rounding.

diacritics.name: Centralized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association (1999), Handbook of the International Phonetic Association, the IPA chart (diacritics)
diacritics.reason: The chart defines ◌̈ as centralized: the vowel moves to the central column, which is [-front, -back]. PanPhon's rule for it changes no feature.

diacritics.name: Advanced tongue root
diacritics.source: Lindau (1978), 'Vowel features', Language 54(3): advanced tongue root is a feature of its own, not the tense/lax distinction
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes ATR as [+tense]. Here [tense] marks vowel height, so ATR sets [+atr] and leaves [tense] as the base has it.

diacritics.name: Retracted tongue root
diacritics.source: Lindau (1978), 'Vowel features', Language 54(3): advanced tongue root is a feature of its own, not the tense/lax distinction
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes RTR as [-tense]. RTR sets [-atr] and leaves [tense] as the base has it.

diacritics.name: Pharyngealized
diacritics.source: McCarthy (1994), 'The phonetics and phonology of Semitic pharyngeals', in Keating (ed.), Papers in Laboratory Phonology III: pharyngealization is a retraction of the tongue root
diacritics.reason: PanPhon's rule gives [+low, +back], but a high base keeps [+high], so [+low] cannot mark the retraction and kˤ equalled k. Pharyngealization sets [-atr] and [+back] on every base.

segments.name: voiced labiodental flap
segments.source: International Phonetic Association, the IPA chart (2005 and later revisions), pulmonic consonants
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the symbol. It is a tap at the labiodental place: the manner of [ɾ] with the place of [v].

segments.name: voiceless epiglottal fricative
segments.source: Esling (2005), 'There are no back vowels: the laryngeal articulator model', Canadian Journal of Linguistics 50: the epiglottal (aryepiglottic) sounds share the pharyngeal place; the fricatives are often trilled
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the symbol. It is the pharyngeal fricative [ħ] made by the aryepiglottic folds, with trilling.

segments.name: voiced epiglottal fricative
segments.source: Esling (2005), 'There are no back vowels: the laryngeal articulator model', Canadian Journal of Linguistics 50: the epiglottal (aryepiglottic) sounds share the pharyngeal place; the fricatives are often trilled
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the symbol. It is the voiced counterpart of [ʜ].

segments.name: epiglottal plosive
segments.source: Esling (2005), 'There are no back vowels: the laryngeal articulator model', Canadian Journal of Linguistics 50: the epiglottal (aryepiglottic) sounds share the pharyngeal place; the fricatives are often trilled
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the symbol. It is a stop at the pharyngeal place, the only stop the IPA chart gives there.
